entities.summary:
The full-scale Russo-Ukrainian war refers to the ongoing conflict between Ukraine and Russia, starting on February 24, 2022, with a full-scale invasion of Ukraine by Russia. This conflict is part of the broader Russo-Ukrainian war, a series of ongoing and sporadic conflicts between the two nations, dating back to 2014.

The full-scale invasion was launched by Russia on February 24, 2022, with a large-scale military operation, involving ground troops, air power, and missile strikes. The conflict has resulted in significant human suffering, displacement of people, and economic damage to Ukraine. The international community has condemned the invasion, with numerous countries imposing sanctions on Russia.

The legacy of the full-scale Russo-Ukrainian war is yet to be fully understood, but it has already led to a significant shift in the global balance of power, with Russia's relations with the West deteriorating further. The conflict has also sparked a new wave of nationalism and militarism in Russia, with President Vladimir Putin's popularity soaring in the country.

As the world watches the unfolding drama, one cannot help but recall the words of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said in a speech to the Ukrainian people, 'We will not give up, we will not lose. We will not give up our land, we will not give up our freedom.'
